messages.author: cb40931b0b653347
messages.subject: Detection probability at truncation distance
parts:
Hello!,

I'm learning how to use distance sampling packages (Distance, mrds, Distance2) for estimating guanacos density and abundance in central Chile. I fitted some models, but i'm having problems to determine the detection probability at truncation distance (or other given distance), i tried to use predict functions from mrds and Distance2 (i know that this last package is still being developed, but i tried it for the analysis i nedded and it worked fine), however, i have different errors. Maybe i'm not using the apropiate function for this?

My errors:

#A model and 2 given distances in a data frame:
>gu2.hn <- ds(DisGua, truncation=350)
>new.df <- data.frame(Total=c(1, 350))

#i had to use ::: because, for some reason, and despite mrds and Distance2 are installed and working, the predict functions don't work
>mrds:::predict.ds(gu2.hn, new.df)

Error in meta.data$binned & !binned : 
  operations are possible only for numeric, logical or complex types

#trying with Distance2 it will returns the average detection probability, i need those from the data frame
>Distance2:::predict.ds(gu2.hn, new.df)
[1] 0.5967605 0.5967605  

#as i said, despite packages are installed and other functions working, this error occurs:
> predict.df(gu2.hn, new.df)
Error: could not find function "predict.df"

I tried changing the R version, with versions 3.1.1, 3.1.3, 3.4.2, 3.4.4. For example, this error happens when using version 3.4.4:

> mrds:::predict.ds(gu2.hn, new.df)
Error in if (ddfobj$type == "unif") { : argument is of length zero

I would be very grateful if anyone could help me with this, i just want to know the detection probability at a given distance. Sorry my english.

Regards!

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Detection probability at truncation distance
parts:
José

Have a look at this discussion from February 2018 on the subject of estimated detection probability at a given perpendicular distance

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/distance-sampling/yEn7i-Js-8A

If you have no covariates in your detection function, you can create a graph of the detection function (using plot.ds()) and read the value of interest from the graph.  More sophisticated work could be done to write a function to compute the desired quantity given the estimated parameters of the detection function if you needed greater precision.
